question: According to the manual, what is the minimum tread depth required in every major groove on front tires?
explanation: The manual states you need at least 4/32-inch tread depth in every major groove on front tires, and 2/32 inch on other tires.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.1 — Vehicle Inspection

question: Which type of tire is prohibited on the front wheels of a bus?
choice_c: Tires with a mismatched tread pattern
explanation: The manual lists regrooved, recapped, or retreaded tires on the front wheels of a bus as prohibited.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.1 — Vehicle Inspection

question: Steering wheel play of more than how many degrees can make a vehicle hard to steer?
explanation: The manual states steering wheel play of more than 10 degrees (about two inches of movement at the rim of a 20-inch wheel) can make it hard to steer.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.1 — Vehicle Inspection

question: A leaf spring is put 'out of service' if what fraction of its leaves are missing or broken?
explanation: The manual states that if one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing from a leaf spring, it will put the vehicle out of service.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.1 — Vehicle Inspection

question: During the in-cab inspection, air pressure should build from 50 to 90 psi within about how long?
explanation: The manual states air pressure should build from 50 to 90 psi within three minutes.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.1 — Vehicle Inspection

question: How many red reflective warning triangles must a commercial vehicle be equipped with?
explanation: The manual lists three reflective warning triangles as required emergency equipment.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.1 — Vehicle Inspection

question: Drivers of trucks transporting cargo must first inspect its securement within how many miles of starting a trip?
explanation: The manual requires drivers to inspect cargo securement within the first 50 miles of a trip, and every 150 miles or three hours after that, whichever comes first.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.1 — Vehicle Inspection

question: When backing, the manual recommends backing and turning toward which side of the vehicle?
choice_b: Whichever side is closer to the curb
choice_c: Either side, it makes no difference
explanation: The manual advises backing toward the driver's side because you can see better and watch the rear of your vehicle through the side window.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.2 — Basic Control of Your Vehicle

question: When starting a manual-transmission vehicle on an upgrade, when should you release the parking brake?
choice_a: Only after applying enough engine power to keep from rolling back
choice_b: As soon as the engine starts
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to release the parking brake only when they have applied enough engine power to keep the vehicle from rolling back.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.2 — Basic Control of Your Vehicle

question: When pulling a trailer, what can rough acceleration damage?
explanation: The manual warns that rough acceleration can damage the coupling when pulling a trailer.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.2 — Basic Control of Your Vehicle

question: If the drive wheels begin to spin while accelerating on poor traction, what should you do?
choice_c: Take your foot off the accelerator
explanation: The manual instructs that if the drive wheels begin to spin, you should take your foot off the accelerator.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.2 — Basic Control of Your Vehicle

question: What technique do most heavy vehicles with manual transmissions require to change gears?
explanation: The manual states most heavy vehicles with manual transmissions require double clutching to change gears.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.3 — Shifting Gears

question: How many basic types of retarders does the manual describe?
explanation: The manual describes four basic types of retarders: exhaust, engine, hydraulic, and electric.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.3 — Shifting Gears

question: When should you turn a retarder off, according to the manual?
choice_b: When the road is wet, icy, or snow covered
explanation: The manual cautions that a retarder can cause drive wheels with poor traction to skid, so you should turn it off whenever the road is wet, icy, or snow covered.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.3 — Shifting Gears

question: Before starting down a hill, the manual says you should generally be in what gear compared to the gear needed to climb the same hill?
choice_a: A higher gear than needed to climb it
choice_b: The same gear as needed to climb it
choice_c: A lower gear than needed to climb it
explanation: The manual states you should downshift before starting down a hill, usually to a gear lower than the one required to climb the same hill.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.3 — Shifting Gears

question: According to the manual, how far ahead should good drivers typically look?
explanation: The manual states most good drivers look at least 12 to 15 seconds ahead.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.4 — Seeing

question: What does the manual recommend to give you a reference point for judging the position of images in your mirrors?
choice_a: Adjust each mirror to show some part of your own vehicle
choice_b: Aim mirrors only at the road surface
choice_d: Angle mirrors upward toward the sky
explanation: The manual recommends adjusting each mirror to show some part of the vehicle, which gives you a reference point for judging other images.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.4 — Seeing

question: What is a key limitation of convex ('fisheye') mirrors noted in the manual?
choice_b: Objects appear smaller and farther away than they really are
choice_d: They are required only on buses
explanation: The manual notes that everything appears smaller in a convex mirror than it would look directly, and things also seem farther away than they really are.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.4 — Seeing

question: When should mirror adjustment be checked for accuracy, per the manual?
choice_c: Prior to the start of any trip, when the trailer is straight
choice_d: Only when parked on a hill
explanation: The manual states mirror adjustment should be checked prior to the start of any trip and can only be checked accurately when the trailer(s) are straight.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.4 — Seeing

question: Which is one of the manual's three rules for using turn signals?
choice_a: Signal only if another vehicle is nearby
choice_c: Use hand signals instead of turn signals
choice_d: Signal early, well before you turn
explanation: The manual's rules for turn signals include signaling early, well before you turn, to keep others from trying to pass you.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.5 — Communicating

question: If you must stop on a two-lane road carrying traffic in both directions, where should you place your warning devices?
choice_a: Within 10 feet of the vehicle, and 100 feet ahead and behind
choice_b: 10, 100, and 200 feet, all toward oncoming traffic
choice_c: 50 feet in front and rear only
explanation: On a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, the manual instructs placing warning devices within 10 feet of the front or rear corners and 100 feet behind and ahead of the vehicle.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.5 — Communicating

question: Within how many minutes of stopping on a road or shoulder must you put out emergency warning devices?
explanation: The manual requires you to put out your emergency warning devices within ten minutes of stopping.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.5 — Communicating

question: Why does the manual advise against signaling other drivers when it is safe for them to pass?
choice_a: It is required at all intersections
choice_b: Only law enforcement should avoid it
choice_c: You could cause a crash and be blamed
choice_d: It is only unsafe at night
explanation: The manual warns you should not direct traffic because you could cause a crash and be blamed for it, at great cost.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.5 — Communicating

question: When passing a vehicle, pedestrian, or bicyclist, how does the manual say you should communicate your presence?
choice_c: Flash your high beams once and hold them on
choice_d: Tap the horn lightly, or at night flash lights from low to high beam and back
explanation: The manual advises tapping the horn lightly or, at night, flashing lights from low to high beam and back when passing.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.5 — Communicating

question: What is the average perception time for an alert driver, and about how far does a vehicle travel during it at 55 mph?
explanation: The manual states the average perception time for an alert driver is 1 3/4 seconds, which at 55 mph accounts for 142 feet traveled.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.6 — Controlling Speed

question: At 55 mph, what is the minimum total stopping distance described in the manual?
explanation: The manual states that at 55 mph, a vehicle will travel a minimum of 419 feet total stopping distance, combining perception, reaction, and braking distance.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.6 — Controlling Speed

question: According to the manual, how much greater is the impact when you double your speed from 20 to 40 mph?
explanation: The manual states that doubling speed from 20 to 40 mph makes the impact four times greater, and the braking distance is also four times longer.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.6 — Controlling Speed

question: On a wet road, the manual recommends reducing speed by about how much compared to dry conditions?
explanation: The manual recommends reducing speed by about one-third, for example slowing from 55 to about 35 mph, on a wet road.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.6 — Controlling Speed

question: According to the manual, hydroplaning can occur at speeds as low as what, if there is a lot of water?
explanation: The manual states hydroplaning can occur at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is a lot of water on the road.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.6 — Controlling Speed

question: At speeds below 40 mph, what following distance rule does the manual give?
choice_b: One second for each 10 feet of vehicle length
explanation: The manual's rule of thumb is at least one second for each 10 feet of vehicle length at speeds below 40 mph.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.7 — Managing Space

question: According to crash reports cited in the manual, what is the most frequent cause of trucks and buses running into the vehicle in front of them?
explanation: The manual states the most frequent cause of trucks and buses running into the vehicle ahead is following too closely.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.7 — Managing Space

question: If you find yourself being tailgated, what does the manual recommend?
choice_b: Flash your brake lights to warn them
explanation: The manual recommends increasing your following distance to help avoid sudden speed or direction changes and to make it easier for the tailgater to pass.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.7 — Managing Space

question: Before backing into an area, what does the manual say you should check for overhead?
choice_a: Overhanging objects such as trees, branches, or electric wires
choice_b: Only the pavement surface behind you
explanation: The manual advises getting out and checking for overhanging objects such as trees, branches, or electric wires before backing into an area.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.7 — Managing Space

question: If your vehicle cannot make a right turn without swinging into another lane, what does the manual recommend?
choice_a: Swing wide to the left as you start the turn
choice_b: Turn wide as you complete the turn, keeping the rear close to the curb
choice_c: Stay tight to the curb the entire turn
explanation: The manual advises turning wide as you complete the turn and keeping the rear of your vehicle close to the curb, to stop other drivers from passing on the right.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.7 — Managing Space

question: How does the manual define a 'hazard'?
choice_a: Only a vehicle already involved in a crash
choice_c: Any road condition or other road user that is a possible danger
explanation: The manual defines a hazard as any road condition or other road user, such as a driver, bicyclist, or pedestrian, that is a possible danger.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.8 — Seeing Hazards

question: When approaching an emergency vehicle stopped on the roadside or a work zone, what does the manual say you should do?
choice_d: Slow down and change into a lane not adjacent to the emergency vehicle or work zone, if safe
explanation: Move-over laws require slowing down and yielding the right-of-way by changing to a lane not adjacent to the stopped emergency vehicle or work zone, when it is safe to do so.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.8 — Seeing Hazards

question: What symbol warns of a slow-moving vehicle such as farm machinery?
choice_a: A red triangle with an orange center
choice_b: A yellow diamond with a black border
choice_d: An orange square with white letters
explanation: The manual describes the slow moving vehicle symbol as a red triangle with an orange center.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.8 — Seeing Hazards

question: How does the manual define being 'in conflict' with another road user?
choice_b: Having to change speed and/or direction to avoid hitting someone
choice_c: Being stuck in a traffic jam
explanation: The manual states you are in conflict when you have to change speed and/or direction to avoid hitting someone.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.8 — Seeing Hazards

question: Why does the manual say you should always have a plan when you see a hazard?
choice_a: To report the hazard to authorities immediately
choice_b: To avoid having to slow down at all
choice_c: To give yourself time to plan a way out of an emergency
explanation: The manual explains that you look for hazards in order to have time to plan a way out of any emergency that could develop.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.8 — Seeing Hazards

question: According to the Large Truck Crash Causation Study cited in the manual, what percent of large-truck crashes occurred when the CMV driver was externally distracted?
explanation: The manual cites the LTCCS finding that 8 percent of large-truck crashes occurred when the CMV driver was externally distracted, and 2 percent when internally distracted.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.9 — Distracted Driving

question: How does the manual define a 'physical distraction'?
choice_a: One that causes you to take your hands off the wheel or eyes off the road
choice_b: One that only involves thinking about something else
choice_c: One that occurs only in bad weather
choice_d: One caused solely by other drivers
explanation: The manual defines a physical distraction as one that causes you to take your hands off the wheel or eyes off the road, such as reaching for an object.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.9 — Distracted Driving

question: How long is a CDL disqualified for a second conviction of texting while operating a CMV within three years?
explanation: The manual states disqualification is 60 days for a second offense within three years, and 120 days for three or more offenses.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.9 — Distracted Driving

question: According to research cited in the manual, texting while driving increases the odds of a safety-critical event by how much compared to not texting?
explanation: The manual states the odds of a safety-critical event are 23.2 times greater for CMV drivers who text while driving than for those who do not.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.9 — Distracted Driving

question: On average, how many seconds does sending or receiving a text take a driver's eyes off the road?
explanation: The manual states sending or receiving a text takes your eyes from the road for an average of 4.6 seconds, the length of a football field at 55 mph.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.9 — Distracted Driving

question: How does the manual define 'road rage'?
choice_a: Operating a vehicle with intent to do harm or physically assault another driver or their vehicle
choice_c: Failing to use a turn signal
explanation: The manual defines road rage as operating a motor vehicle with the intent of doing harm to others or physically assaulting a driver or their vehicle.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.10 — Aggressive Drivers/Road Rage

question: What does the manual recommend if you are confronted by an aggressive driver?
choice_a: Speed up and hold your lane
choice_b: Get out of their way and avoid eye contact
choice_c: Make eye contact to show confidence
choice_d: Flash your high beams at them
explanation: The manual advises first attempting to get out of an aggressive driver's way and avoiding eye contact, rather than challenging them.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.10 — Aggressive Drivers/Road Rage

question: How does the manual define 'aggressive driving'?
choice_a: Exceeding the posted speed limit by any amount
choice_b: Any act resulting in physical assault
choice_c: Operating a vehicle in a selfish, bold, or pushy manner without regard for others' safety
explanation: The manual defines aggressive driving as the act of operating a motor vehicle in a selfish, bold, or pushy manner, without regard for the rights or safety of others.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.10 — Aggressive Drivers/Road Rage

question: If an aggressive driver you were dealing with is later involved in a crash farther down the road, what should you do?
choice_b: Pull the driver from their vehicle
choice_c: Continue your trip and call later
choice_d: Stop a safe distance away, wait for police, and report what you witnessed
explanation: The manual advises stopping a safe distance from the crash scene, waiting for police to arrive, and reporting the driving behavior you witnessed.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.10 — Aggressive Drivers/Road Rage

question: About how far ahead can you see with low-beam headlights at night, per the manual?
explanation: The manual states that with low beams you can see ahead about 250 feet, compared to about 350-500 feet with high beams.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.11 — Driving at Night

question: Within what distance of an oncoming vehicle should you dim your headlights?
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to dim their lights within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.11 — Driving at Night

question: Within what distance of a vehicle you are following should you dim your headlights?
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to dim their lights when following another vehicle within 300 feet.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.11 — Driving at Night

question: According to the manual, what is the only safe cure for being sleepy while driving?
choice_b: Open the window for fresh air
choice_d: Get off the road and sleep
explanation: The manual states that if you are sleepy, the only safe cure is to get off the road and get some sleep.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.11 — Driving at Night

question: If you are momentarily blinded by glare from an oncoming vehicle's bright lights, what does the manual say to do?
choice_a: Look at the right side of the road
choice_c: Flash your own high beams back
choice_d: Speed up to get past it quickly
explanation: The manual advises not looking directly at bright lights and instead looking at the right side of the road.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.11 — Driving at Night

question: What is the best advice for driving in fog, according to the manual?
choice_a: Drive faster to get through it quickly
choice_b: Don't drive in fog if you can avoid it
choice_c: Follow closely behind another vehicle's taillights
explanation: The manual states the best advice for driving in fog is 'don't' — it's preferable to pull off the road until visibility improves.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.12 — Driving in Fog

question: What headlights does the manual recommend using in fog for best visibility?
explanation: The manual recommends using low-beam headlights and fog lights for the best visibility in fog, even in daytime.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.12 — Driving in Fog

question: What does the manual say to use as guides for determining how the road curves ahead in fog?
explanation: The manual advises using roadside highway reflectors as guides to determine how the road may curve ahead of you in fog.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.12 — Driving in Fog

question: What can happen to your brakes when driving in heavy rain or deep standing water?
choice_a: They can become weak, apply unevenly, or grab, possibly causing a jackknife
choice_c: There is no effect on braking performance
explanation: The manual states water in the brakes can cause them to be weak, apply unevenly, or grab, which can cause a jackknife if pulling a trailer.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.13 — Driving in Winter

question: After driving through deep water, how should you dry out your brakes?
choice_a: Apply the parking brake fully and hold it
choice_b: Maintain light pressure on the brakes for a short distance
choice_c: Avoid using the brakes for ten minutes
choice_d: Pump the brakes as hard as possible
explanation: The manual instructs maintaining light pressure on the brakes for a short distance after crossing water, to heat them up and dry them out.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.13 — Driving in Winter

question: The manual suggests an easy way to check for ice while driving is to open the window and feel what?
choice_c: The front of the mirror, mirror support, or antenna
explanation: The manual recommends opening the window and feeling the front of the mirror, mirror support, or antenna to check for ice buildup.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.13 — Driving in Winter

question: What does a lack of spray from other vehicles' tires indicate, according to the manual?
choice_a: Vehicles are driving faster than normal
choice_b: Vehicles are using their hazard lights
choice_c: There is increased spray from other vehicles
choice_d: Ice has formed on the road
explanation: The manual states a lack of spray from other vehicles indicates that ice has formed on the road.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.13 — Driving in Winter

question: Why does the manual advise against using the engine brake or speed retarder on slippery winter roads?
choice_a: They can cause the driving wheels to skid
choice_d: They are illegal to use in winter
explanation: The manual warns that the engine brake or speed retarder can cause the driving wheels to skid on slippery surfaces.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.13 — Driving in Winter

question: How often should you inspect your tires when driving in very hot weather?
explanation: The manual recommends inspecting the tires every two hours or every 100 miles when driving in very hot weather.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.14 — Driving in Very Hot Weather

question: What should you do if a tire is too hot to touch?
choice_a: Let air out to reduce pressure
choice_c: Remain stopped until the tire cools off
choice_d: Pour water directly on the tire
explanation: The manual states that if a tire is too hot to touch, you should remain stopped until it cools off, or it may blow out or catch fire.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.14 — Driving in Very Hot Weather

question: What does 'bleeding tar' on the road surface indicate, according to the manual?
explanation: The manual notes that tar rising to the surface in very hot weather creates spots that are very slippery.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.14 — Driving in Very Hot Weather

question: How does the manual define a 'passive' railroad-highway crossing?
choice_a: A crossing with no traffic control device, leaving the decision up to the driver
choice_b: A crossing with gates and bells
choice_c: A crossing controlled by a flagman
choice_d: A crossing found only in cities
explanation: The manual describes a passive crossing as one without any type of traffic control device, where the decision to stop or proceed rests entirely with the driver.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.15 — Railroad-Highway Crossings

question: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, what does the manual instruct you to do?
choice_a: Stay in the vehicle and call for help
choice_b: Evacuate and walk toward the oncoming train, away from the tracks at a 45-degree angle
choice_c: Try to push the vehicle off the tracks alone
choice_d: Run alongside the tracks in either direction
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to evacuate the vehicle and walk in the direction of the oncoming train, away from the tracks at a 45-degree angle.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.15 — Railroad-Highway Crossings

question: About how long does it take a typical tractor-trailer unit to clear a single railroad track?
explanation: The manual states it takes a typical tractor-trailer unit at least 14 seconds to clear a single track, and more than 15 seconds for a double track.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.15 — Railroad-Highway Crossings

question: What should you do when the flashing red lights at a crossbuck sign begin to flash?
choice_a: Speed up to cross before the train arrives
choice_b: Proceed with caution at reduced speed
explanation: The manual states that when the lights begin to flash, you must stop because a train is approaching and you are required to yield the right-of-way.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.15 — Railroad-Highway Crossings

question: What should you do with the transmission before starting down a long, steep grade?
choice_a: Shift to a low gear before starting down the grade
choice_c: Keep the same gear used on flat roads
choice_d: Shift to a higher gear for smoother descent
explanation: The manual instructs shifting the transmission to a low gear before starting down the grade, since downshifting after speed has built up may not be possible.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.16 — Mountain Driving

question: How does the manual describe 'brake fade'?
choice_a: When brakes lock up suddenly without warning
choice_b: When you must apply the brakes harder and harder to get the same stopping power
choice_c: When the brake pedal squeals loudly
choice_d: When brake fluid freezes in cold weather
explanation: The manual describes brake fade as needing to apply the brakes harder and harder to get the same stopping power due to excessive heat.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.16 — Mountain Driving

question: What is the purpose of an escape ramp on a mountain downgrade?
choice_a: To provide a shortcut down the mountain
choice_b: To serve as a truck weigh station
choice_c: To stop runaway vehicles safely without injuring drivers or passengers
choice_d: To provide a scenic rest stop
explanation: The manual explains that escape ramps are made to stop runaway vehicles safely without injuring drivers and passengers.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.16 — Mountain Driving

question: In the manual's example, if your 'safe' speed on a downgrade is 40 mph, to what speed should you let the brakes reduce your speed before releasing them?
explanation: The manual's example has you apply the brakes at 40 mph to gradually reduce speed to 35 mph, then release the brakes and repeat as needed.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 2.16 — Mountain Driving
